fichas.title: Transport planning
fichas.summary: Transport is part of material flow. Planning defines transport relationships and tasks, and their interactions with storage. Essential terms include transported goods, transport performance, transport type, and means of transport. Means of transport are divided into continuous and discontinuous conveyors.

fichas.title: Continuous conveyors
fichas.summary: Continuous conveyors move goods along a defined permanent or mobile route between loading and unloading locations. They suit similar goods transported over a fixed route; high automation and capacity are balanced by high investment and low adaptability. Types shown or listed include belts, track and chain conveyors, screw conveyors, slides, overhead chain and rope conveyors, moving tables, pneumatic conveyors, centrifugal conveyors, and bucket chain conveyors.
uses: Continuously move bulk materials and unit loads
Transport similar goods over a fixed route

Continuous conveyors
Continuous conveyors are mechanical, hydraulic or pneumatic
systems with a defined transport route (permanent or mobile),
along which the transported goods are continuously (regularly, in
cycles or with variable speed) moved between loading and unloading locations. Continuous conveyors are particularly suitable
for the transport of similar goods over a fixed route, but the high
automation and transport capacity comes at the cost of high investment and low adaptability.

Continuous conveyors include:
Conveyor belts -> 0, track and chain conveyors -> 0, screw
conveyors, slides -> 0, endless overhead chain and rope conveyors, moving tables -> 0, pneumatic (pressure and suction)
conveyors (bulk goods and liquids), centrifugal conveyors and
bucket chain conveyors.
Discontinuous conveyors
Discontinuous conveyors work discontinuously. They can be differentiated into industrial trucks (running on wheels on a floor) and
lifting devices (mostly cranes).

Floor conveyors
Industrial trucks are manually or mechanically driven, mostly without being on tracks, for stacking heights up to 6 m, in special cases up to 10 m. The advantages are the low plant costs and good
suitability for medium distances between unloading and loading
locations on a flat road or floor.

fichas.title: Discontinuous conveyors and floor conveyors
fichas.summary: Discontinuous conveyors operate intermittently and include industrial trucks running on wheels on a floor and lifting devices, mostly cranes. Floor conveyors are manually or mechanically driven, usually not track-bound, and are suited to medium distances on flat floors or roads. The text gives typical and exceptional stacking heights.

fichas.title: Cranes
fichas.summary: Cranes lift large and heavy goods vertically; horizontal movement may be provided by wheeled or winch trolleys. Swivel cranes lift objects from any point within their operating radius. The page illustrates wall- and column-mounted swivel cranes, gantry cranes, runway catwalks, and safety dimensions.
uses: Lift large and heavy goods vertically
Handle loads within a swivel crane's operating radius
